No credential literals in source. Read secrets from the environment or a secret manager.
Pin third-party GitHub Actions to a full commit SHA; a tag or branch is a mutable pointer.
Declare least-privilege `permissions:` in every workflow; never `write-all`.
Never run a composed string through a shell. Pass argv.
Confine paths with Path.is_relative_to, not a string prefix check.
Validate archive members before extraction; extractall writes anywhere its names point.
Catch the exceptions you can handle; never swallow everything silently.
Every network call needs an explicit timeout, or it hangs forever by default.
Bound subprocess calls with a timeout so a wedged child cannot hang the run.
Validate environment variables at startup rather than failing with a KeyError deep in a call.
Do not log values held in secret-named variables.
Pin dependency versions exactly so a build is a function of its lockfile.
A mutable default argument is shared across every call.
Use an explicit guard and a raised error, not assert — assertions vanish under -O.
Containers must declare a non-root USER.
Pin base images to a digest or an exact version, never `latest`.
Never interpolate an attacker-controllable workflow expression into a `run:` script.
Shell scripts need `set -euo pipefail`, or they continue past a failed command.
Quote shell variable expansions; unquoted ones word-split on spaces and vanish when empty.
eval and exec run arbitrary code; parse or convert explicitly instead.
Use select() rather than the legacy session.query() API.
A blocking call inside `async def` stalls the whole event loop.
Use the logger the module already imports, not print — print contaminates stdio.
No privileged containers, no privilege escalation, no uid 0.
Pin package.json dependencies exactly; a range resolves differently per environment.
Discarding an error with `_ =` turns a failure into silent corruption.
Build temporary paths with mktemp, not $RANDOM or a timestamp.
A pull_request_target workflow must state the ref it checks out.
eval() executes arbitrary JavaScript; use JSON.parse or an explicit dispatch.
Compare to None with `is`, not `==` — equality can be overloaded.
Keep a reference to a created task, or it can be garbage-collected mid-flight.
Install dependencies before copying source, or every source edit reinstalls them.
Use console.debug for developer output; console.log reaches the user.
A discarded subprocess result means the exit code was never examined.
Piping a download straight into a shell runs whatever the server sent, unverified.
